preamble: Making a line look like a heading and making it *be* a heading are two different things. You could make the text bigger and bold and it would read fine on screen — but Docs wouldn't know anything had changed. A heading is a label you attach to a line, saying "this starts a section." The larger, bolder look is just what that label happens to look like. You're about to attach the label, not paint the text.
generalization: The formatting you get is a side effect. What you actually did was tell Docs the structure of the document — and now the outline pane knows about this line, a table of contents would pick it up, a PDF export would carry the structure across, and changing your heading look once changes every heading at once. That's the difference between styling text and describing it: description scales, decoration doesn't.

steps.intent: The toolbar has two kinds of control side by side: ones that change how text looks, and one that changes what the text is. That second kind is a single box, and it always shows the current line's role in the document — right now it almost certainly reads "Normal text," which is Docs' way of saying "just prose." Open it to see the other roles a line can have.
hints: Skip past the bold, italic and size controls — those only affect appearance. You want the one control that names the line rather than decorating it.
Toolbar, left-hand end, just right of the undo and redo arrows — a wide box showing 'Normal text'.

wrongHints.Bold: Reasonable, since headings are bold. But bold is paint: Docs would still file this line as ordinary prose, and no outline or contents would ever find it.
wrongHints.Font size: Headings are bigger, so this looks like the right lever. Size is a property, though, not a role — Docs can't tell a large sentence from a section title.

steps.intent: The list you're looking at is a hierarchy, not a set of sizes. Heading 1 is the top level — the beginning of a major section. Choosing it tells Docs this line opens a section, and everything below it until the next Heading 1 belongs to it.
hints: You're picking a rank, not a look. Which entry means 'top-level section' rather than 'the name of the whole document'?
In the open dropdown, below 'Title' and 'Subtitle', above Heading 2 and Heading 3.

wrongHints.Title: It sits at the top of the list and looks the grandest, so it's a fair guess. But Docs reserves Title for the name of the document as a whole — it doesn't create a section, so it won't behave like a heading in the outline or a contents list.
